result.title: Functional Depth Is Learned: Isolating the Computation That Layers Produce Only Together
result.summary: Transformer performance scales with depth, but layer count merely counts the opportunities for sequential computation: layers could still behave as nearly independent refinements that barely depend on one another. We study how transformers develop functional depth during pretraining, introducing an exact inclusion-exclusion decomposition that isolates the connected component, i.e., the computation that appears only when a specified set of layers acts together under identity ablation. Tracking this quantity across public checkpoints of Pythia, OLMo, and Amber yields three findings. First, write-relative connected coordination strengthens from its initialization or earliest-checkpoint baseline as pretraining proceeds, across all measured interaction orders. Second, these connected components are behaviorally consequential under direct intervention: deleting them damages perplexity more than deleting a norm-matched random direction at the same site in all 35 measured model-order cells. Third, pairwise representation similarity is consistently negatively correlated with pairwise connected coordination across seven models, yet the two signals are not interchangeable: similarity- and coordination-based block-removal criteria often agree in Pythia but diverge on Amber. Together, these results suggest that architectural depth provides the opportunity for sequential computation, while pretraining progressively organizes cross-layer dependencies within that depth.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 inclusion-exclusion 精确分解，度量仅当指定层共同作用时才出现的「连通计算」，并在 Pythia、OLMo、Amber 的公开 checkpoint 上追踪其随预训练增强、对困惑度的因果影响及与成对表示相似度的负相关。
AI.relevance_reason: 其连通计算分解与 identity ablation 可供核查 LVR 中深度收益与跨层贡献分配，并提示表示相似度不等同于实际跨层依赖；但论文对象是纯文本语言模型，多模态与 latent 推理联系需自行迁移。
